video_goal: Demonstrate how to physically insert a SIM card and verify cellular network connection on a US-unlocked Google Pixel 10.
required_subjects_and_props: US-unlocked base model Google Pixel 10, metal SIM ejector tool, nano-SIM card, wooden desk

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands pick up a base model Google Pixel 10 from a wooden desk, briefly tilting it to reveal the distinctive horizontal rear camera bar.
The phone is held sideways to expose the bottom edge. The right hand brings a metal SIM ejector tool toward the small circular hole next to the USB-C port.
The tip of the SIM ejector tool presses firmly into the hole, causing the SIM tray to pop out about two millimeters.
The thumb and index finger pinch the protruding edge of the SIM tray and pull it completely out of the phone chassis.
The empty SIM tray rests on the desk. Fingers carefully align and drop a nano-SIM card into the tray, ensuring the gold contacts face upward and the angled corner matches the tray's shape.
Fingers guide the loaded SIM tray back into the bottom slot of the Pixel 10, pushing it until it sits perfectly flush with the metal frame.
The right thumb presses the side power button. The Pixel 10 screen illuminates, displaying the default lock screen.
A finger swipes up from the bottom of the screen to unlock the device, then taps the gear-shaped 'Settings' app icon on the home screen.
The finger taps the 'Network & internet' option located at the very top of the Settings menu.
The finger taps the 'SIMs' menu item, transitioning to a screen that displays the newly recognized cellular carrier's name with a toggle switch turned on.
The camera focuses on the top right corner of the phone's status bar as the hollow signal triangle fills with solid white bars and a '5G' logo appears.
The user holds the fully set up Google Pixel 10, swiping back to the home screen while the active cellular signal remains visible in the top right corner.
